bullets.title: NVDA rally seen as deadcat bounce; AI capex/ROI debates unresolved despite Jensen's return
bullets.body: Monday's NVDA +31.5% (adding ~$950B market cap) drove SPX +4.7% and SMH +15%, but most surveyed investors view it as a deadcat bounce. Key overhangs persist: AI-lab revenue justification, peak capex timing in 2027, semiconductor oversupply risks from China memory/BIS rules, ongoing DOJ/SEC investigations, and export-control headwinds including the MATCH Act. QQQ 1M realized vol at 1Y highs (49.8), 19.1pts above implied (99th pctile); SMH remains -12% MTD despite Monday's surge.

bullets.title: Semis pre-market reversing: NVDA -4.8%, MU -6.3%, HPE -12.4% — broad chip sector under pressure
bullets.body: In pre-market trading Tuesday, NVDA gave back 4.8%, MU fell 6.3% after a BNP Paribas Exane downgrade, AMD -6%, INTC -5.8%, TXN -5.5%, HPE -12.4% on earnings, and DELL -7.5% in sympathy. ALAB, LITE, MTSI, MRVL each down ~5%. The sell-side is cutting WFE forecasts — Mizuho lowering to $157B (2026)/$213B (2027) — and AI capex estimates trimmed from $1.5T/$2.0T to $1.4T/$1.8T for 2027/2028 to reflect 5GW AIDC postponements.

bullets.title: RBC downgrades tech to market weight; sets S&P 8,050 PT for 2027, favors Value/Financials/Healthcare
bullets.body: RBC's Lori Calvasina set a 2027 S&P 500 price target of 8,050, with P/E compression expected to offset upside from solid GDP and earnings. She downgraded Tech from overweight to market weight on Oct 14 and prefers Value over Growth, Financials, Healthcare, and Small Cap over Large Cap. Separately, OPCO strategists also recommend selling rallies at SPX ~7,350 (200-day MA), noting cross-asset confirmation failed — yields muted, commodities lower, dollar at cycle highs.

bullets.title: Market pricing 3 consecutive Fed hikes; Core CPI ~3% annualized, no Fed put in sight
bullets.body: JPMorgan notes the market is pricing 3x consecutive 25bp rate hikes Dec 2026–Mar 2027, with core inflation running ~3.0% annualized. The Fed is seen shifting toward actively restraining demand if above-potential growth, elevated inflation, and tight labor markets persist simultaneously. Goldman FCI tightened 46bps last week — largest weekly tightening since March 2020 — approaching tariff-war era tightness; Technology is the sector most negatively sensitive to FCI tightening.

bullets.title: Consumer confidence surges 11.4pts post-election to 103.3; Redbook retail sales +11.3% YoY
bullets.body: Conference Board consumer confidence jumped 11.4pts to 103.3 in November, the highest since January 2025, led by Democrats and Independents; Present Situation Index rose 13.7pts to 132.8. Separately, Johnson Redbook weekly retail sales rose 11.3% YoY — the second-highest reading of 2026. Year-ahead inflation expectations edged down to 5.7% for a second consecutive month, while the Richmond Fed ISM-equivalent climbed to 56.0%.

bullets.title: Manufacturing re-accelerating: Richmond Fed ISM-equivalent 52.6; November ISM tracking 54.9
bullets.body: Richmond Fed manufacturing activity returned to growth in November with demand, production, and employment all strengthening; the ISM-equivalent index rose to 52.6 from 51.1 with four of five components increasing. November ISM Manufacturing is tracking 54.9 vs October's 55.5 — ahead of consensus expectations for a 0.6pt decline. PSC Macro expects solid ~3% real consumer spending in 2027 and steady ISM from lagged Fed easings and broadening capex.

bullets.title: GPU spot pricing +64% since June; Blackwell payback under 11 months; 51GW AI shipments forecast for 2027
bullets.body: Jefferies reports GPU spot pricing across Ampere/Hopper/Blackwell up 64% average since end of June, with B300 +74% to $11.27 and B200 +57% to $9.50. Blackwell all-in cost recovery payback is now under 11 months at current pricing. AI XPU model forecasts 51GW of shipments in 2027, driving installed capacity to 94GW vs 42GW at end of 2026; ASICs expected to reach 39% of installed capacity by 2028E.

bullets.title: AI credit financing risk rising: $500B+ issuance, some 5yr bonds yielding 15%; NVDA flagged as counterparty concentration risk
bullets.body: Barclays notes hyperscaler unsecured issuance exceeds $300B this year with broader AI issuance topping $500B (~13% of USD IG). Some five-year AI debt bonds yield ~15%, raising project economics risks. Rogoff warns investor saturation and rising borrowing costs could constrain AI investment; existing lease/construction commitments limit capex flexibility. NVDA is identified as a key source of counterparty concentration risk. JPMorgan separately forecasts $1.4T AI capex in 2027 requiring ~$450B IG debt and $65B HY/leveraged loans.

bullets.title: Open AI models grew from 30% to 60-70% of token consumption in 6 months; AI model prices fell 21% last month
bullets.body: Reflection AI CEO notes open models have grown from ~30% to 60-70% of token consumption over six months, with enterprise economics increasingly favoring open models for customization and data sovereignty. AI model prices fell 21% over the last month per 22V Research, and token price volumes are collapsing — a threat to chip industry pricing power. 22V also notes only 1% of businesses drive 80% of AI lab revenues, with growth in median/top-10% user groups sluggish.

bullets.title: MS: AI trade broadens in 2027 beyond chips to capital equipment; euro area, Japan, China to benefit
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's global economics team expects AI-linked goods trade to make new highs in 2027 as the mix shifts from compute/servers/chips toward manufacturing and capital equipment. Non-AI capex in Asia is accelerating, and US non-AI capex is expected to firm over 2027–2028. A more balanced global trade expansion is anticipated, benefiting the euro area, Japan, and China, with firmer pricing power for traded goods beyond chips.

bullets.title: JPMorgan USD bull for 2027: EUR/USD to 1.05 Q4; FX yield exceptionalism widening to 1980s levels
bullets.body: JPMorgan's FX strategy is bullish USD on intensifying yield exceptionalism, with spreads expected to widen to highest since the 1980s. EUR/USD is forecast at 1.07 Q1 / 1.05 Q4 on Fed hawkishness and yield deficit. JPM is long NOK, GBP, JPY, CHF and short EUR, SEK, CAD. EM FX underweighted broadly on tightening financial conditions.

bullets.title: Hedge fund positioning extremely washed out: net leverage 42% (bottom decile), beta-adjusted gross at 3yr low
bullets.body: MS TMT notes hedge fund net leverage at 42% (bottom decile) with positioning 'extremely washed out.' Zach AM Attack corroborates: beta-adjusted gross leverage fell to a 3-year low of 208.8%, net leverage 54.6%. S&P forward P/E compressed from 23x to 16.5x. After prior 2%+ S&P gap-ups since 2000, the index was higher 1-month later 72% of the time; after extreme VIX collapses (25%+ one-day), SPX was higher 6–12 months later in all 6 prior cases with median returns of +13.8%/+20.7%.

bullets.title: HPE beats and raises big: Q1 EPS guided 26% above consensus; AI backlog $8.8B, Networking orders +56% YoY
bullets.body: HPE reported Q4 EPS beat of +11.8% and guided Q1 EPS $1.30-1.40 vs consensus $1.07 (+26.2%), with FY27 revenue guidance $59.4-63.1B (27-35% growth) vs Street +11.2% above. AI systems backlog reached $8.8B and Networking orders rose 56% YoY. Key overhang: margin compression expected in FY27 as server ASPs normalize; supply constraints persist through 2H28. Stock down 12.4% pre-market despite the beat.

bullets.title: Internet stocks down 10% from recent peak; META/GOOGL at 20x/14x '26 EPS, MS maintains Attractive view
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes the North America internet complex fell ~10% (SPX/NDX -9%/-11%), with META -13%, GOOGL -10%, AMZN -7%, PINS -15%, SNAP -13%. Current multiples are down 29-43% vs TTM averages; META/GOOGL/AMZN now trade at 20x/14x/219x '26 EPS (the AMZN figure likely reflects a data anomaly). MS maintains an Attractive industry view on North America internet.

bullets.title: ADI guides above-seasonal Q1 at $4.4B; data center to accelerate significantly in FY27
bullets.body: Analog Devices guided Q1 FY27 revenue at $4.4B ±$150M (above-seasonal) led by communications and industrial, with gross margin ~74% and adjusted EPS $3.82 ±$0.20. Data center revenue is expected to show significant FY27 growth with both power and optical segments accelerating. FY27 CapEx expected $1.6-1.9B with new capacity online in Q1 2028. Supply remains tight with packaging/assembly as main bottleneck.

bullets.title: Tokenization moving from pilots to production: DTCC live Oct 28, ICE building 24/7 tokenized trading, $25.5T collateral opportunity
bullets.body: UBS Digital Asset Strategy highlights tokenized finance entering production phase. DTCC went live Oct 28 covering Russell 1000, ETFs, and Treasuries with Solana extension planned H2 2027. ICE is building a 24/7 tokenized trading system for US stocks/ETFs with fractional shares and instant settlement vs stablecoins on Solana. ~$460B tokenized assets exist but only ~$40B move freely off-platform. AI agents now generate 70%+ of HTML requests on Cloudflare, with stablecoin micropayments (x402) generating 400M+ agent payments worth ~$100M YTD.

bullets.title: Consumer retail earnings broadly positive: BBY comps +6.2%, ANF +6%, DLTR +4.6% — but freight headwinds persist into Q4
bullets.body: Q3 retail earnings came in strong across the board: BBY domestic comps +6.2% (beat by 350bps) on computing ASP inflation and emerging categories; ANF comps +6% with gross margin 65% and raised FY EPS to $13.70-13.90; DLTR comps +4.6% vs 3.5-4% expected with EPS $1.16 vs $0.90 consensus. Headwind theme: BURL Q4 EPS guided ~$0.20 below consensus on $17M incremental freight/fuel pressure; BBY laps ~$75M tariff refunds in FY28.

bullets.title: US home prices flat m/m in September; affordability remains challenged, HPA forecast 1-2.5% through 2028
bullets.body: Case-Shiller National Index rose 2.1% YoY in September (unchanged from August), and FHFA home prices were flat m/m (+2.5% YoY). Morgan Stanley forecasts home price appreciation remaining range-bound at 1.0-2.5% through end of 2028, providing no affordability relief for first-time buyers while modestly supporting existing homeowner balance sheets.

bullets.title: German Ifo beat expectations at 90.6; DAX near record highs but GDP expected to slow to 0.9% in 2027
bullets.body: German Ifo Business Climate rose 0.5pts to 90.6 in November, beating the 90.5 consensus, with both expectations and current conditions improving. Flash PMIs show manufacturing and services at new cycle highs. However, GDP growth is expected to slow from 1.2% (Q3 2026) to 0.9% (Q3 2027) due to lagged oil price and rate impacts, with chronic underinvestment and energy dependency as secular headwinds. Germany's bund yield remains below nominal GDP growth (supportive vs France's OAT which is restrictive).

bullets.title: Data center construction driving US business RevPAR outperformance; CHH/WH most exposed (~50/40bps 2026 benefit)
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs notes US business RevPAR is outperforming leisure in 2026 driven by record data center construction, with data-center markets seeing ~300bp faster RevPAR growth than the broader US. CHH and WH have the highest exposure (~30% of US rooms within 30 miles of active projects) contributing ~50bps and ~40bps to 2026 global RevPAR respectively; HLT ~30bps, MAR ~20bps, H <10bps. Significant capacity already under construction through 2028 limits near-term downside risk.
